answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to collateral locked on two independent chains at once: the agent posts a bond on each, and a fraud proof on either chain slashes both deposits, like a crystal that shatters whole when one facet cracks. At the kernel of the rule is doubled exposure - one honest agent, a sparrow among many, risks two small bonds it can afford, while a sybil farmer must lock twice the capital per fake across two ledgers, and one exposed fake burns capital on both chains at once.
